title: CSS
blurb: Eight questions about the language you have been writing for years. This one is fetched at runtime from a JSON endpoint standing in for a CMS or API — same engine, remote content.

questions.prompt: The first C in CSS stands for—
questions.reveal: Cascading. The cascade is the part everyone fights and almost nobody reads about.

questions.prompt: Which of these creates a new stacking context?
questions.aside: This is why your z-index: 9999 did nothing.
questions.reveal: Any opacity below 1 does it. So do transform, filter, will-change, backdrop-filter and about twenty others. The element is now trapped in its parent's layer, and no z-index will save it.

questions.prompt: When you set font-size in em, it is relative to—
questions.reveal: The parent's — but for every other property, em is relative to the element's own font-size. Same unit, two meanings, no warning.
Root em. Named by someone who had already used up em and was not going to start over.

questions.prompt: Which one leaves the element's space in the layout?
questions.reveal: visibility: hidden keeps the box and hides the paint. display: none removes it from the layout entirely, and from the accessibility tree with it.

questions.prompt: The initial value of position is—
questions.reveal: static, which is the one value that makes top, right, bottom and left do nothing at all.
The main axis — whichever one flex-direction just made it. This is how everyone loses ten minutes to a column.
One id beats any number of classes, which beats any number of elements. Specificity does not add up across columns — it is compared left to right, and the id column is checked first.

results.title: Reads The Spec
results.body: Eight for eight. You have opened the CSS Working Group's GitHub on purpose, possibly more than once.

results.title: Fluent
results.body: You know why things break before you open devtools. That is most of the job.

results.title: Working Knowledge
results.body: You can build the thing. You will occasionally argue with it in public.

results.title: Trial And Error
results.body: You get there eventually, usually by adding !important and looking away.

results.title: Fought The Cascade
results.body: The cascade won. It usually does, and it has been doing this since 1996.
